title: BizFlood Claims Adjusting Guide — Coverage on the Date of Loss, Coinsurance, Business Income and Payment
content:
**Settlement rule.** A claim under BizFlood Commercial Flood Policies (Surplus Lines) is covered only when the date of loss falls inside the term and on or after the location's effective date. Each location is adjusted on its own. When the location's limit is below the tier's coinsurance percentage of its value at the time of loss and agreed value is not in force for the term, the building or contents payment is the loss multiplied by the limit divided by the coinsurance percentage of that value, rounded to the cent, less the deductible; otherwise it is the loss less the deductible; each is never below zero and capped at the limit. On the BizFlood Excess over NFIP tier the loss is first reduced by the attachment. Business income is paid for the loss after the tier's business income waiting period in elapsed hours and within the tier's longest period of restoration in calendar months, up to the business income limit, with extra expense within the tier's extra expense percentage of it. The proof of loss is due within the tier's proof of loss period in calendar days of the date of loss, payment within the tier's payment period in calendar days of agreement, and a new payment is the payable amount less what has been paid net of voids.

## Building and contents payment, defined

For one location and one coverage (building, or contents):

1. On BizFlood Excess over NFIP only, the loss is first reduced by that location's attachment for the coverage.
2. **Coinsurance test** — compare the limit with the coinsurance percentage of the location's value at the time of loss. The coinsurance formula is used when both hold: the limit is below that figure, and agreed value is not in force for the term.
3. **Payment where the formula is used** — the loss multiplied by the limit, divided by the coinsurance percentage of the value, rounded to the cent, and then less the deductible.
4. **Payment otherwise** — the loss less the deductible.
5. The result is never below zero and never above the limit.

| Limit below the coinsurance figure | Agreed value in force for the term | Payment |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | Loss multiplied by limit, divided by the coinsurance figure, rounded to the cent, less the deductible |
| Yes | Yes | Loss less the deductible |
| No | No | Loss less the deductible |
| No | Yes | Loss less the deductible |

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures; coinsurance percentage of 80 percent; deductible 10,000)

| Case | Value at loss | Limit | Loss | Payment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Under-insured, no agreed value | 1,000,000 | 600,000 | 200,000 | Coinsurance figure 800,000; 200,000 multiplied by 600,000, divided by 800,000, is 150,000.00; less 10,000: 140,000.00 |
| Same, agreed value in force | 1,000,000 | 600,000 | 200,000 | 190,000.00 |
| Limit exactly at the coinsurance figure | 1,000,000 | 800,000 | 200,000 | Not below, so 190,000.00 |
| Large loss | 1,000,000 | 800,000 | 900,000 | 890,000.00 capped at the limit: 800,000.00 |
| Small loss | 1,000,000 | 800,000 | 6,000 | Below zero, so 0.00 |

On BizFlood Excess over NFIP, a hypothetical building loss of 1,200,000 at a location with a 500,000 building attachment is first reduced to 700,000, and the test and payment above then work on 700,000.

## Business income and extra expense

Business income is paid for the loss after the waiting period in elapsed hours, counted from the direct physical loss, and within the longest period of restoration, up to the location's business income limit. Extra expense is paid within the extra expense percentage of the business income limit. For a hypothetical business income limit of 1,000,000 and an extra expense percentage of 25 percent, extra expense is paid within 250,000.

## Time limits and further payments

- The proof of loss is due within the proof of loss period, in calendar days, of the date of loss; payment is due within the payment period, in calendar days, of agreement.
- A new payment on a claim, for one coverage, is the payable amount less what has already been paid on that claim and coverage net of voids — payments issued over the life of the claim less payments voided. For a hypothetical payable amount of 140,000.00, with 100,000.00 issued earlier and 10,000.00 of that voided, the net paid is 90,000.00 and the new payment is 50,000.00.
